title: Small Language Models (SLMs) Deployment
summary: Deploy compact models for bounded tasks where local control, latency, or operating cost matters and measured capability is sufficient.
overview: Small language model deployment places a comparatively compact model into a serving environment suited to a defined task. Small is relative to the model family and workload; parameter count alone does not determine latency, memory, or quality. Tokenizer, architecture, context length, precision, hardware, and serving engine all affect the operating envelope.

Compact models often fit classification, extraction, routing, or constrained drafting better than open-ended complex reasoning. The architecture should narrow the task contract, provide relevant evidence, and validate outputs. A local small model is not automatically private or safe: logs, telemetry, updates, and tool access still need explicit controls.

production.poc: A prototype benchmarks the candidate on real task examples and the intended hardware, including failure cases.
production.production: Production packages weights, tokenizer, runtime, and configuration as a versioned artifact with health checks and bounded concurrency.
production.scale: Enterprise scale adds fleet update controls, hardware-specific evaluation, monitoring of quality drift, and an approved fallback for tasks beyond the model’s envelope.

components.name: Model artifact registry
components.role: Stores approved weights, tokenizer, license information, and evaluation metadata.

components.name: Local inference runtime
components.role: Executes the model with compatible kernels and resource limits.

components.name: Task adapter
components.role: Constrains prompts, schemas, and input sizes to the evaluated task.

components.name: Output validator
components.role: Rejects malformed or unsupported results and selects escalation.

components.name: Fleet manager
components.role: Distributes signed versions and observes health across deployment locations.

flow.title: Define a narrow task
flow.description: Specify supported inputs, output schema, quality thresholds, and escalation conditions.

flow.title: Benchmark on target hardware
flow.description: Measure startup, latency, memory, and quality under representative concurrency.

flow.title: Package the runtime
flow.description: Pin the model, tokenizer, quantization, and engine as one tested release.

flow.title: Serve bounded requests
flow.description: Apply input limits, resource admission, and local authorization.

flow.title: Validate outputs
flow.description: Use schema and task-specific checks before results reach downstream systems.

flow.title: Update through cohorts
flow.description: Roll out to a small fleet segment and compare quality and resource use before expansion.

useCase.title: Classifying operator inspection notes
useCase.situation: A factory workstation classifies short inspection notes into approved defect categories during intermittent connectivity.
useCase.problem: Cloud dependence delays local triage, while unrestricted generation is unnecessary for the classification task.
useCase.requirement: Run a bounded local classifier with explicit unknown handling and synchronized quality monitoring.
useCase.architecture: A compact model uses a constrained category schema and stores uncertain cases for review.
runtime: An operator note is classified locally and validated against the approved taxonomy.
An unfamiliar defect description receives an unknown status rather than a forced category.
useCase.failure: If an update increases unknown or incorrect classifications, the workstation returns to the previous model bundle.
useCase.impact: Measure per-category recall, unknown handling, local latency, and memory footprint; lower model size does not excuse lower task acceptance.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces network dependency and data transfer.

tradeoffs.cost: Limits flexibility beyond the approved workload.
Requires hardware-specific quality and speed validation.

failures.detection: Latency and memory rise under simultaneous requests.
failures.recovery: Limit admission and queue bounded work.

failures.detection: Unknown and error rates rise for a new product line.
failures.recovery: Review examples and update the model or task taxonomy.

mistakes.fix: Benchmark the complete runtime on target hardware.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming local means no data egress
mistakes.fix: Inspect telemetry, update, and logging paths.

mistakes.mistake: Forcing an answer on every input
mistakes.fix: Provide an explicit unknown or escalation outcome.

whenToUse: Use for narrow high-volume tasks with clear labels.
Use for constrained or intermittently connected environments.
Use when local latency and control justify fleet operations.
whenNotToUse: Do not deploy without target-hardware evaluation.
Avoid local models when maintenance cost exceeds the benefit.
checklist: Test fleet rollback and offline behavior.
